name: Xia Hua
current_role: Chairwoman, Eve Group (依文集团), Beijing; founder of Eve China Handmade; vice chair, All-China Chamber of Commerce (ACFIC); NPC deputy
profile: Xia Hua (夏华) left a law lectureship at China University of Political Science and Law to found menswear company Eve (依文) in 1994, building it into a leading Chinese menswear brand. She now focuses on Eve China Handmade, which links rural ethnic-minority embroiderers in Guizhou, Yunnan and Sichuan with global fashion through digital pattern libraries and IP licensing.
interesting_fact: Her China Handmade platform works with more than 25,000 rural embroiderers; she cites a Miao artisan, 'Grandma Pan', whose family embroidery business earns over 1.8 million yuan a year.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Eve she quit her teaching post and became a shop-floor salesperson at a Xidan mall in Beijing, becoming its top seller within a month by studying which stores' bags shoppers carried. She later funded an 'Eve Distinguished Professor' fund at her alma mater CUPL (2003).
notes: High-profile public figure in China (NPC deputy, ACFIC vice chair, frequent Xinhua interviewee); best route is via Eve Group corporate office. Hurun listing 'Eve' = 依文.

name: Ye Jiahao
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2016-2020) as founder/owner of Qixin Construction; current role not verified
profile: Ye Jiahao (叶家豪) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2016-2020 with wealth attributed to 'Qixin Construction' (construction sector). Web searches in Chinese and English found no public coverage linking him to a specific company, so identity and current role could not be confirmed.
notes: Very low public profile; company name 'Qixin' may be a romanisation of 祺鑫/启鑫/奇信 etc. Verify via Chinese business registry (e.g. Qichacha) before outreach.

name: Dinesh Kumar Goel
current_role: Founder Chairman & Chief Mentor, FIITJEE Ltd (New Delhi)
profile: D.K. Goel, an IIT Delhi mechanical engineering graduate, founded FIITJEE (Forum for IIT-JEE) in 1992, building it into one of India's largest coaching chains for IIT-JEE and science olympiads, with centres in India, Bahrain and Qatar. Since late 2024 the company has faced centre closures and regulatory investigations.
interesting_fact: FIITJEE's name is an acronym: 'Forum for Indian Institute of Technology - Joint Entrance Examination'; the company was incorporated as FIITJEE Limited in 1997, five years after Goel started it.
notes: Caution: in 2024-25 FIITJEE shut multiple centres; Delhi Police EOW cheating case and Enforcement Directorate raids (April 2025) over student fees, which Goel denies; also a 2024 leaked staff-meeting video. Reputational risk for a podcast guest.

name: Shi Weixue
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2016-2021) as owner of 'Guowei' (real estate, investments); current role not verified
profile: Shi Weixue (史维学) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2016-2021 with wealth attributed to 'Guowei' in real estate and investments. Chinese and English web searches returned no coverage linking him to an identifiable company, so identity and current role are unconfirmed.
notes: Very low public profile; Baidu Baike blocked from this environment. Verify company (国伟?) via Chinese business registry before outreach.

name: Qiu Guang
current_role: Chairman & CEO and controlling shareholder, Shenzhen Riland Industry Group (瑞凌股份, SZSE: 300154)
profile: Qiu Guang (邱光) founded Shenzhen Riland, a maker of inverter welding and cutting equipment sold under the Riland, Rilon, HiTronic and T&R brands. Riland listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in December 2010; Qiu remains chairman, CEO and actual controller, with the company now expanding into laser welding and robotic/intelligent welding systems.
interesting_fact: Riland was the first company in China's domestic inverter welding equipment industry to list on the A-share market (ChiNext, December 2010).
deep_cut_fact: Known in Western trade press as 'Simon Qiu', he signed a 2014 cooperation deal with German welding-robot maker CLOOS at the Beijing Essen Welding & Cutting fair, under which Riland produces machines in China under CLOOS quality control.
notes: Email is Riland's published marketing-department address (not a dedicated press/IR desk); the site also has an investor-relations section and online message form. Hurun lists wealth shared with Qi Xuexia.

name: Starr Wisdom
current_role: Co-trustee of the Albert Erani Family Trust; member of the Organogenesis (ORGO) controlling shareholder group in SEC filings
profile: Starr Wisdom is a reporting person in the Schedule 13D group (with Alan Ades, Albert and Dennis Erani, Glenn Nussdorf and related trusts) that controls Organogenesis Holdings, a regenerative-medicine/wound-care company. SEC filings show she personally held only about 20,000 ORGO shares; the large '10% owner' value reflects her role as a co-trustee of family trusts in the group, not an operating business she founded.
notes: Private individual, not an entrepreneur or public figure; wealth figure is an artefact of trustee/group reporting (SEC 13D/A, e.g. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1661181/000119312521156648/d474086dsc13da.htm). Not a suitable podcast target; Organogenesis IR would be the only institutional route.

name: Yang Liangzhi
current_role: Chairman, Richinfo Technology Co., Ltd. (彩讯股份, SZSE: 300634), Shenzhen
profile: Yang Liangzhi (杨良志) leads Richinfo Technology, a Shenzhen software company founded in 2004 that built its business as an operating partner for China Mobile's 139 Mailbox and enterprise email, later expanding into digital marketing, cloud and collaboration software. Richinfo listed on ChiNext in March 2018; Yang was re-elected chairman of the fourth board in 2025 and the company now pushes its Rich AIBox AI application platform.
interesting_fact: Richinfo is the operations partner behind China Mobile's '139 Mailbox' consumer email service, which grew out of its mobile-email products around 2009.
notes: Founder status per one secondary source (altss.com) only. Hurun lists wealth shared with Wang Haihong. IR handled by board office (board secretary Wang Xin per 2025 filings); use Shenzhen exchange/cninfo IR channels.

name: George C Zoley
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, The GEO Group, Inc. (NYSE: GEO), Boca Raton, Florida
profile: Greek-born George Zoley founded what became The GEO Group in 1984 as Wackenhut Corrections Corporation, a division of Wackenhut, and led it as CEO from its 1994 IPO until 2021 and again later, building one of the largest US operators of private prisons, immigration detention and electronic-monitoring services. He is now Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: He received the Ellis Island Medal of Honor in 2002, which recognises immigrants and descendants of immigrants for contributions to American life.
deep_cut_fact: Born George Zolis in Florina, Greece, in 1950, he moved to Ohio with his mother and sister at about age three and went to public high school in Copley, Ohio; he holds three public-administration degrees (BA, MA from Florida Atlantic, doctorate from Nova Southeastern) and later chaired FAU's board of trustees.

public_contacts.value: Pablo E. Paez, EVP Corporate Relations, The GEO Group, (866) 301-4436 (published media contact)

notes: GEO is politically controversial (private prisons/ICE detention); a 2013 FAU stadium naming deal with GEO was withdrawn after protests. Media requests go through Corporate Relations (in-house, not an agency).

name: Yao Zhongliang
current_role: Party Secretary, Chairman and President, Baixiang Food Co., Ltd. (白象食品), Henan; deputy to the 14th National People's Congress
profile: Yao Zhongliang (姚忠良), born 1962 in Pingyu, Henan, left the army in 1983 for local grain bureaus and in 1996 became general manager of the Baixiang instant-noodle factory, turning it into one of China's leading domestic noodle brands. He still runs the company as chairman and president and is an NPC deputy and vice chair of the Henan Federation of Industry and Commerce.
interesting_fact: About one-third of Baixiang's employees are people with disabilities; when this was reported during the 2022 Beijing Winter Paralympics, consumers bought its noodles en masse in support and the brand went viral.
deep_cut_fact: Before noodles, Yao was a soldier who, after leaving the military in 1983, worked his way up through a county and then a regional grain bureau; he was named a National Model Worker in 2010 and carried the torch for the 2023 Chengdu Universiade.
notes: Low personal media profile despite brand fame; company refers to disabled staff as 'self-improvement staff'. Route via Baixiang corporate office (Zhengzhou).

name: Lyu Genmi
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2014) as owner of 'Wantong' (construction); current role not verified
profile: Lyu Genmi (吕根觅) appeared once on the Hurun China Rich List (2014) with wealth attributed to 'Wantong' in construction. No web coverage of the name was found in Chinese or English, so the company and current status could not be confirmed.
notes: No public footprint found; not related to Beijing Vantone (万通发展) as far as searches show. Verify via Chinese business registry before any outreach.

name: Yu Jianmo
current_role: Major shareholder (approx. 11.6% in 2023) of Dalian Meijimu Education Technology (*ST美吉, SZSE: 002621); former chairman, left board March 2017
profile: Yu Jianmo (俞建模) was the long-time chairman and a core shareholder of SZSE-listed 002621, originally Dalian Sanlei (plastic-pipe machinery), which later pivoted into early-childhood education by acquiring the China operator of the US My Gym children's fitness brand and was renamed Meijimu (美吉姆). He stepped down as chairman and director in March 2017 and has since been reducing his stake.
interesting_fact: The company he led reinvented itself from industrial machinery into children's education, taking over the China franchise of the US kids' gym brand My Gym.
notes: No longer in management; low public profile. Hurun lists wealth shared with Yu Yang. Company is now *ST (risk warning) status. Sanlei-machinery background is from memory of company history, verify in SZSE filings.

name: Zheng Bingxu
current_role: Long-time chairman and party secretary of Guangdong Hongda Blasting (now Guangdong Hongda Holdings, SZSE: 002683), confirmed in post through end-2021; current role not verified
profile: Zheng Bingxu (郑炳旭), born 1959, a PhD and professor-level senior engineer, ran Guangdong Hongda Blasting Engineering Company from 1988 and built it into a listed mining-services, civil-explosives and defence-equipment group, serving as chairman/GM from 2010 and chairman from 2016. In 2019 he held about 6.33% of the company.
interesting_fact: Under his chairmanship in December 2021, Hongda agreed to co-found the Guangdong Province Military Industry Group with the national industry investment fund and provincial partners, marking its push from blasting into defence equipment.
deep_cut_fact: He became general manager of the then-state-owned Guangdong Hongda Blasting Engineering Company in 1988 at about 29, and stayed with the business for over three decades, also holding the title of chief technical expert, unusual for a chairman.
notes: Engineer-executive of a state-linked company; may have retired after 2021 (check latest 002683 announcements). Route via Hongda board office.

name: Liang Wei
current_role: Controlling shareholder/actual controller of Wuhan Golden Laser (金运激光, SZSE: 300220); no longer a director or executive
profile: Liang Wei (梁伟) was chairman and general manager of Wuhan Golden Laser from 2009 and took it public on ChiNext in 2011; the company makes laser cutting/engraving systems and moved into 3D printing. He has since left the board and management but remains the controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Golden Laser, the Wuhan laser-equipment maker he led, listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in 2011 and later diversified into 3D printing applications.
notes: Not suitable for outreach: in August 2026 the Jiangsu High Court upheld his conviction for securities-market manipulation (3 years 9 months, RMB 12m fine). Common name; identity tied via Golden Laser.

name: Zheng Kanghao
current_role: Founder, Chairman & President of Shenzhen Wongtee Group (宏泰集团, since 1997); director (former chairman 2010-2022) of Shenzhen Wongtee International Enterprise
profile: Zheng Kanghao (郑康豪) founded Shenzhen Wongtee Group, a Shenzhen real-estate developer, in 1997 and chaired its listed affiliate Shenzhen Wongtee International Enterprise from 2010 until 2022, when he stepped back to director. Third-party databases also list him as head of Wongtee's real-estate development arm and chairman of a Shenzhen investment fund company.
notes: Roles sourced only from MarketScreener insider pages (https://marketscreener.com/insider/KANG-HAO-ZHENG-A11HSA); company websites unreachable. Very low media profile.

name: Fu Shuangli
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Zhejiang Yingfeng Technology Co., Ltd. (迎丰股份, SSE: 605055), Keqiao, Shaoxing (re-elected Dec 2025)
profile: Fu Shuangli (傅双利) built Yingfeng into one of the large textile printing-and-dyeing groups in Shaoxing's Keqiao textile hub, listing it on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2021. He remains chairman, general manager and legal representative, and also chairs Light Textile City Printing & Dyeing, in which Yingfeng holds a stake.
interesting_fact: Yingfeng specialises in dyeing and finishing high-end functional and multi-component fabrics (anti-UV, flame-retardant, waterproof) at its Binhai industrial-zone plant in Keqiao, China's largest light-textile trading hub.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond running a dye house, he sits on the board of the Keqiao Weaving & Dyeing 'Industry Brain' operating company, a digital platform for the local dyeing cluster, and heads Shaoxing Lianran Software Technology.
notes: IR email is the board secretary's office address published in the 2024 annual report (board secretary at the time Ni Huifang; a new secretary was appointed Dec 2025). Hurun lists wealth shared with Ma Yingbo (company director).

name: Wang Shi
current_role: Co-actual controller and shareholder of Guangdong Biolight Meditech (宝莱特, SZSE: 300246), Zhuhai
profile: Wang Shi (王石, a woman; not the Vanke founder of the same name) is, together with chairman and president Yan Jinyuan, the actual controller of Guangdong Biolight Meditech, a Zhuhai maker of patient monitors, haemodialysis equipment and consumables. She held about 2.5% directly in 2025; in 2026 the controllers transferred about 7% of the company to Zhejiang Quwei Zhihe Holding.
interesting_fact: Biolight (宝莱特) is a Zhuhai-based medical-device maker that expanded from patient monitoring into kidney-dialysis products and services.
notes: Not an operating executive; chairman Yan Jinyuan (Hurun co-listee) is the public face of Biolight and the better podcast target. Do not confuse with Vanke's Wang Shi.

name: Huang Zhiming
current_role: Founder and former chairman/GM of Chengdu Xinzhu Road & Bridge Machinery (新筑股份, SZSE: 002480); no longer chairman (2026 chairman is Zhou Fenggang)
profile: Huang Zhiming (黄志明), from Chengdu, founded Xinjin Xinzhu Road & Bridge Machinery in 1996 to make road and railway bridge components, converted it into a joint-stock company in 2001 and took it public in Shenzhen. Its railway bridge bearings long led the Chinese market. The company has since passed to new (state-linked) control and he no longer chairs it; his current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Xinzhu's railway bridge bearings held the top market share in China for years, and the company helped draft national and industry standards for bridge functional components.
deep_cut_fact: He served as a vice chairman of the board of Southwest Jiaotong University and on the committee of the Mao Yisheng Science and Education Fund, named after China's pioneering bridge engineer; his motto: 'quality cost is the company's first cost, talent capital its first capital.'
notes: Exit from Xinzhu leadership date not verified; check 002480 filings c.2018-2019. Low current profile.

name: Yang Xiaoming
current_role: Former chairman and actual controller of Yuancheng Cable (远程电缆 / 远程股份, SZSE: 002692), Yixing, Jiangsu; now a reduced minority shareholder (approx. 6% in 2022)
profile: Yang Xiaoming (杨小明), from Guanlin in Yixing, Jiangsu (a major Chinese cable-making cluster), was chairman, controlling shareholder and actual controller of Yuancheng Cable when it listed in Shenzhen around 2012. He later handed the chair to Yu Guoping, lost part of his stake through a court-ordered execution in 2020 and sold down further in 2021-22.
interesting_fact: Yuancheng Cable is based in Guanlin town, Yixing, one of China's densest wire-and-cable manufacturing clusters.
notes: No longer runs the company, which has carried an ST (risk-warning) tag; stake reductions involved judicial enforcement. Low suitability for outreach; current activities unknown. Common name - identity tied via SZSE filings.

name: Chen Shaomei
current_role: Legal representative, head and ultimate controller of Guangdong VTR Bio-Tech (溢多利, SZSE: 300381), Zhuhai
profile: Chen Shaomei (陈少美) is the actual controller and legal representative of Guangdong VTR Bio-Tech, founded in Zhuhai in 1991, which grew into a leading Asian producer of industrial and feed enzymes and later expanded into steroid pharmaceutical intermediates and animal health. Day-to-day management sits with president/CEO Zhou Derong (since 2022); Chen's parent company held about 29% in 2025.
interesting_fact: VTR describes itself as Asia's largest bio-enzymes producer, with 11 manufacturing bases, 85 invention patents and sales in more than 60 countries.
notes: Hurun romanises the company as 'VTR' (溢多利 / Yiduoli). IR email is the board secretary (Zhu Shanmin) contact in the 2025 interim report. Low personal media profile.

name: Ren Shuliang
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, China Maple Leaf Educational Systems (HKEX: 1317) (per Aug 2025 board list)
profile: Ren Shuliang (任书良), known internationally as Dr. Sherman Jen, founded the first Maple Leaf International School in Dalian in 1995, pioneering a dual-diploma model that pairs the British Columbia (Canada) curriculum with Chinese education. Maple Leaf grew into a large network of bilingual K-12 schools and preschools in China and Southeast Asia and listed in Hong Kong in 2014; he remains chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: Maple Leaf schools teach the British Columbia provincial curriculum, so graduates earn a BC Dogwood diploma alongside Chinese credentials; by October 2020 the group operated 114 schools.
deep_cut_fact: In 2017 he personally gave C$5 million to Thompson Rivers University in Kamloops, BC, the largest private donation in its history, funding a high-fidelity simulation centre, an instrumentation lab, a research innovation fund and scholarships.
notes: Goes by 'Sherman Jen' in English (Shu Liang Sherman Jen in HKEX filings); strong Canadian (BC) ties - Canadian universities (TRU, Royal Roads) are a warm angle. IR email from 2019 annual report, may be dated; info@ is the schools' general inbox.
